confirmed.title: Holding a keyframe diamond for its menu fails if the finger drifts even 1px, and a press slightly off-centre moves the keyframe
confirmed.see: On the phone, the only way to delete a keyframe or change its easing is to hold its diamond until the menu appears. If his finger drifts by even 1px during the hold (real fingers always do), the menu never appears. If he pressed a few pixels off the diamond's centre but still inside its touch area, the keyframe also jumps to where his finger is (3.000 s went to 3.133 s, four frames) and that move is saved to undo. So he keeps trying to delete a keyframe, can't, and it creeps sideways each time. That matches his #625 complaint: 'sometimes I try to delete them and I can't'.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a holding a keyframe diamond for its menu fails when the finger trembles, and nudges the keyframe instead. Fails with: he held the keyframe diamond for 0.65 s to delete it or change its easing, his finger drifted 1px, and the menu never opened — on the phone that hold is the only way in; AND the same hold moved the keyframe from 3.000 s to 3.133 s — a press a few pixels off the diamond centre plus one pixel of drift retimes it, and the release records it in undo. (Control in the same test: a perfectly still hold does open the menu.)
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:4724 `kfDrag.moved = true;` runs on ANY pointermove after the hold arms: there is no slop, unlike the trim grip's 8px or the pre-arm 10px. js/timeline.js:4706 `let nt = Math.round(timeFromX(e.clientX) * fps) / fps;` puts the keyframe at the finger's ABSOLUTE position, not relative to where the press landed. The diamond's touch pad is 35px around an 11px shape (styles.css:3241 `.kf-dot::after { inset: -12px }`), so a press up to about 17px off-centre is normal. On pointerup (js/timeline.js ~4858), `moved` means a drag gets committed with FM.history.commit() and the `armed && !moved` menu branch never runs.
confirmed.fix: After arming, only treat the gesture as a drag once the finger has travelled about 6px from downX/downY; below that, keep it a hold so the release opens the menu. Make the retime relative: nt = orig + (clientX - downX) / pxPerSec(), snapped to a frame. That way the keyframe cannot jump to the finger.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug, and I reproduced it. I served the worktree on port 8901 and ran the test with ?only=HUNT-a holding a keyframe. It fails with exactly the reported message. The control in the same test passes: a trusted touch, landing on .kf-dot, held still for 0.65 s, does open the Delete-keyframe menu. So the route works in the harness, and only the tremor breaks it.

The code path in js/timeline.js confirms it:
(1) The pointerdown on a diamond (~2618) arms kfDrag after KF_HOLD_MS = 320 ms. The menu opens only on RELEASE, and only through the `else if (armed)` branch at ~4876, which runs when `moved` is false.
(2) In the window pointermove handler (~4704-4732), the pre-arm phase has a 10 px slop from downX/downY. After arming there is none: `kfDrag.moved = true;` runs on any pointermove at all, and `nt = Math.round(timeFromX(e.clientX) * fps) / fps` writes the finger's ABSOLUTE time into kf.t.
(3) On pointerup (~4869), moved===true takes the drag branch. That runs dedupDraggedKfs, rebuild and FM.history.commit(), so the menu never opens and the retime lands in undo.

So a hold that sees any movement between the colour change and lift-off loses the menu. If the press landed off-centre inside the 35 px touch pad (.kf-dot::after inset -12px around an 11 px shape), the keyframe also jumps to the finger. At phone zoom, 8 px moved it from 3.000 s to 3.133 s.

This state is easy to reach. Ezra is on iPhone (REQUESTS.md says "his iPhone"). WebKit delivers touchmove/pointermove for any contact movement and has no slop of its own. A finger resting for ~0.5 s, and especially one lifting off, routinely shifts its contact point by a pixel or more. That is exactly why the pre-arm check already allows 10 px and the trim grip allows 6 px. The fixture is also reachable: a selected shape with Move/Transform open makes that property's diamonds live, as the diamond's own comments describe. Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for zero slop after arming. The "every pixel from here retimes" comment is about drag responsiveness, not a request of his.

Two caveats. The title's "the only way to delete/ease on the phone" is slightly overstated: the inspector's keyframe toggle at the playhead is another route. And the exact 1 px figure depends on the device delivering sub-slop moves. Neither changes the verdict: the hold-to-menu gesture on the phone fails on ordinary finger drift, and it silently retimes the keyframe and commits that to undo. That is a user-facing defect consistent with his #625 wording.

I edited nothing. The only change was stopping the port-8901 server afterwards (its exit code 144 is that kill).

confirmed.title: A sideways swipe that starts on a keyframe diamond does nothing, and the keyframe at the playhead sits right in the middle of the timeline
confirmed.see: With a layer selected and its property editor open (e.g. Move & Transform), its keyframe diamonds are live, each with an invisible touch area about 35px wide. When he has just set a keyframe, that diamond sits under the playhead in the centre of the timeline. His next swipe to move along the timeline usually starts there, and nothing happens: no scrub, no scroll. An 80px swipe from the diamond moved the playhead 0.00 s; the same swipe elsewhere on the clip moved it 1.92 s. This is the #699 dead-strip bug again, this time on the diamonds. It only happens with a layer selected, so it probably feeds his still-open #768 ('scrubbing with a layer selected is jumpy').
confirmed.test: HUNT-a a sideways swipe that starts on a keyframe diamond does not scrub — the middle of the timeline goes dead. Fails with: an 80px sideways swipe that started on the keyframe diamond under the playhead moved the playhead 0.00 s, where the same swipe on the clip moves it 1.92 s — with a keyframe at the playhead the middle of the phone timeline is dead to his thumb. (Control: the same real-touch swipe on the same clip, clear of the diamonds, scrubs more than 0.5 s.)
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:2599 the diamond's pointerdown calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.preventDefault();` and captures the pointer on the dot. That means the clip's clipTap and the #timeline scrub (js/timeline.js:4428, which also excludes `.kf-dot`) never see the finger. Then js/timeline.js:4717 `if (moved > 10) { ... kfDrag = null; }` drops the gesture when the finger moves before the hold arms, and nothing takes over the swipe. The comment there calls it 'a scrub past the diamond', but no scrub is started.
confirmed.fix: When the finger travels more than 10px before the hold arms, hand the gesture to the scrub instead of dropping it: create `scrub` from kfDrag.downX/downY and the current FM.time, set dragging = true, and capture the pointer on innerEl. Every later move then runs the normal scrub or vertical-pan branch. A throwaway version of exactly this turned the test green.

confirmed.title: Flicking the layer list up or down from a clip or a layer name stops dead the moment his finger lifts; only bare lane glides
confirmed.see: #415 ('Scrolling up and down on timeline should have some glide to it like dragging left and right') is marked done, but the glide only works if the flick starts on bare lane between clips. In a real project nearly every row is mostly clip, and the layer column on the left is where you'd naturally scroll from. A flick from either of those stops dead on release (147 px to 147 px from a clip, 132 to 132 from a layer name), while the identical flick from bare lane keeps going about 80px. So scrolling a long layer list on the phone feels sticky and needs many short swipes.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a flicking the layer list up from a clip or a layer name stops dead — only bare lane glides. Fails with: the same upward flick that glides 82px from bare lane does not glide at all from anywhere else: from a clip the list stopped dead the moment his finger lifted (147 -> 147px); from a layer name it stopped dead too (132 -> 132px) — on a full timeline almost every flick starts on a clip or a name. (Control: the bare-lane flick is checked to be a trusted touch on .track-lane and to glide more than 20px.)
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:4620 the clipTap vertical branch only does `timelineEl.scrollTop = clipTap.startScrollTop - dy` and records no velocity. confirmed.title: Touching the timeline to stop a glide also selects the clip under his finger, which collapses the timeline to one row and opens the edit sheet
confirmed.see: He flicks the timeline sideways and touches it to stop at the spot he wants. The glide does stop (queue 823 c9), but that same touch counts as a tap. The clip under his finger gets selected, the phone timeline collapses to that one row, and the edit sheet comes up. Catching a glide costs him his view and a tap-off to get back. Everywhere else on the phone, a touch that stops a moving list doesn't count as a tap.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a touching the timeline to stop a glide selects the clip under the finger and throws up the edit sheet. Fails with: he flicked the timeline and touched it to stop the glide — it stopped, but the same touch selected HUNT g1, the timeline collapsed to that one row and the edit sheet came up, so every catch of a glide costs him his view and a tap-off. (Controls: the playhead is confirmed to be gliding when the touch lands, the touch is a trusted press on a .clip, and a plain tap with nothing gliding must still select.)
confirmed.evidence: js/timeline.js:4375 `timelineEl.addEventListener('pointerdown', () => { stopMomentum(); stopScrollMomentum(); ... }, true)` stops the glide but doesn't record that the press caught one. On the phone a selection switches to the solo row (soloLayerId) and raises the sheet.
confirmed.fix: In the capture-phase pointerdown, record whether a horizontal or vertical momentum rAF was running (momentumRAF || scrollMomRAF) before stopping it. In the clipTap release, skip the select when that press caught a glide. The same flag should stop the bare-lane tap-to-deselect in that case. A plain tap on a still timeline must keep selecting; the test checks that too. A throwaway version turned the test green.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I re-ran the test against the worktree already being served on port 8901. That worktree is HEAD 3b420976 plus a commit that only adds tests, so the app code is what he has now. - The capture-phase pointerdown at js/timeline.js:4375 calls stopMomentum() and stopScrollMomentum() but records nothing about whether a glide was running.
- The clip's touch pointerdown at 2135 always creates a fresh clipTap with moved:false.
- On release, line ~4801 runs `if (!ct.moved) ... FM.selectLayer(ct.layer.id)`, so the touch that caught the glide counts as a plain tap. On the phone that selects the clip, collapses the timeline to its one row, and (per the queue 707 comment next to it) opens the sheet under his finger.

He will hit this for real. queue 103 made the glide longer on purpose: friction 0.947 gives about 1.5 s of glide after a hard flick, and the timeline is mostly clips, so most touches to stop a glide land on one.

The test's controls hold up:
- It checks the playhead was really moving before the touch.
- It checks the touch was a trusted touch that landed on a .clip.
- It checks a plain tap with nothing moving still selects.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for a touch that stops a glide to also select. queue 823 c9 is a hunt finding, not his words, and it framed the stopping touch that selects as a problem. The fix there only made the glide stop.

Small caveats, which do not change the verdict:
- The test does not check the edit sheet itself; that part rests on how the phone handles any selection.
- A fix needs a small speed threshold, so a tap made as a glide fades out still selects.
- The empty-lane tap-to-deselect at ~4779 has the same gap: touching bare lane to stop a glide also deselects.

This is a real bug. I re-ran the test against the hunt-d worktree on port 8904 and it failed with the same message. Both of its controls passed: an export with nothing isolated showed both squares, and the preview was isolated.

How the code produces it:
- The compositor reads FM.isolate inside FM.renderScene (js/compositor.js:15530, and :15567 for mode 1).
- The exporter calls that same function on FM.scene itself, not on a copy. The MP4, GIF and PNG-frames paths all do this (js/exporter.js:907, 1387 and 1451).
- Nothing on the way to an export clears the isolate. That covers showExportDialog, showExportDialogNow and runExport (js/app.js:4858-5440).
- Only two things clear it: selecting a different layer (js/app.js:3039) or cycling the button back (js/app.js:6654).

He can reach this on PC:
- The desktop Export button stays visible while a clip is selected. The phone-only m-editing rule that hides #m-export does not apply at desktop width.

Pinch-zoomed 3x it is nearly twice as soft (23.7 px). The same blur without the key measures 20 px at every scale. He tunes the softness on a preview that does not match the file. Glow on a keyed clip goes the same way, because it is a drop-shadow length in the same filter string.

Fails with: a Blur on a green-screened clip is 13.0 px soft in the export but 8.6 px in the phone preview (scale 0.58), 3.3 px in the playback tier (scale 0.3), 23.7 px in a 3x zoomed preview — he judges the softness on a preview that does not match the file (the same blur without the key is 20.0 px everywhere)
confirmed.evidence: js/compositor.js:14465 `ctx.filter = effectFilter(layer, t, renderScale(ctx));` builds the blur in TARGET device pixels (:1858 `'blur(' + (nn('radius', 6) * S) + 'px)'`). The media branch then bakes that string into the key offscreen, which is in SOURCE pixels: :14800 `src = chromaKey(src, w, h, p.color || '#00ff00', tol, ctx.filter, cks, ckd)` and :14806 lumaKey(..., ctx.filter, ...). Inside chromaKey (:1429) `octx.filter = filterStr; octx.drawImage(src, 0, 0, w, h)`. The keyed source is then drawn through the render-scale transform (:14814), so the radius is multiplied by the render scale twice. Controls: the unkeyed blur measures 20 px at 1, 0.58, 0.3 and 3x, and the key really removes the green.
confirmed.fix: Build the filter string for the key offscreen in source pixels: divide the lengths by the source-to-device scale (renderScale times the layer's effective scale; getTransform().a at the draw is the honest number). Or draw the keyed source unfiltered and apply the filter at the final drawImage, where device pixels are correct.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test in the hunt-d worktree on port 8904 and it failed the same way the hunter reported. On a keyed clip the blur measures 13.0 px in the export, 8.6 px at the 0.58 phone scale, 3.3 px at the 0.3 playback tier and 23.7 px at 3x zoom. The same blur with no key measures 20.0 px at every scale, so the ruler is sound, and the test checks that the key really removes the green.

I read the code path and it matches the report. At js/compositor.js:14444 the filter is built as `ctx.filter = effectFilter(layer, t, renderScale(ctx))`. Blur there is `radius * S`, measured in the target canvas's device pixels. That is correct for the unkeyed case, because ctx.filter works in device pixels and ignores the canvas transform (see the v6.16 note above renderScale at :3373-3390).

When a Chroma Key or Luma Key is on, the media branch (:14800 and :14806) hands that same ctx.filter string to chromaKey or lumaKey. Those functions apply it to an offscreen canvas the size of the source (w,h = m.width,m.height at :14700): `octx.filter = filterStr; octx.drawImage(src,0,0,w,h)` at :1429. The code then sets ctx.filter to 'none' and draws the keyed source through the render-scale transform. So the blur length is multiplied by the render scale twice. The effective blur is radius × renderScale, when it should be the radius alone. Glow is a drop-shadow length in the same filter string, so it has the same fault.

He can reach this in normal use:
- **Phone preview:** previewScale in js/app.js:471-491 gives a scale below 1 for most projects. For example, a 1080-wide project in a 250 CSS px stage at dpr 3 comes out at about 0.87.
- **Playback:** the playback tiers (PLAY_TIERS 0.8 down to 0.28) lower it further while the video plays.
- **Pinch-zoom:** the zoom crop at app.js:542-552 raises it to as much as 6.
- **Desktop:** a large window at dpr 2 renders above 1.

The export always renders at 1, so the preview softness does not match the file. That contradicts what v16.90 (#913.5) told him: that zooming no longer changes effects, "even blurs", and the zoomed view is exactly what exports.

The fixture is fair. The test draws through FM.renderScene with the same __fmRS, __fmOX, __fmOY and __fmCrop values the real preview canvas sets. It uses no synthetic input events, and the render is synchronous, so timing is not involved. The export reading being narrower than the unkeyed 20 px is expected: the filter runs before the key, the Alight Motion order the code comment describes, so the key removes some of the blurred ramp.

REQUESTS.md holds nothing that makes this intended. There is also no existing test of keyed blur at different scales.

A related point, not needed for this verdict: the offscreen works in source pixels, so a keyed clip with a layer scale other than 1, or a source resolution that differs from the project, is wrong even in the export.

confirmed.title: A mask added from Effects slides up and left of where he drew it while Motion Blur is on and the layer moves
confirmed.see: He adds Motion Blur to a moving clip and masks it with Effects → Mask. While the clip moves, the masked window shows 17 px left and 18 px up of the outline he drew. The offset grows with speed, up to a quarter of the frame. It snaps back to the right place when the clip stops, so the reveal jumps. It happens the same way in the preview and in the export, and the mask editor's outline does not match the picture.

Fails with: with Motion Blur on, the mask he added from Effects shows through 123,82 to 161,122 instead of the 140,100 to 180,140 he drew — it slides 17 px left and 18 px up while the layer moves, in the preview and the export, and snaps back when it stops
confirmed.evidence: js/fx-browser.js:520 creates every Effects mask as a marker `{ type: 'penmask', maskId }`. Motion Blur (Object) dispatches outermost (js/compositor.js:14421) into a plate padded by the travel: :3010-3011 `const m = … Math.min(Math.ceil(_travel) + 2, PW * 0.25)` and `plate.__fmOX = -m; plate.__fmOY = -m`. The marker is then applied inside that plate by drawPenMaskAt (:2882). nestedPlate returns OX = -m, but maskAlphaAt (:2887, js/masks.js:129) builds the stencil with project (0,0) at pixel 0 and knows nothing of the origin, and it is stamped at the plate origin: :2899 `octx.drawImage(maskCanvas, OX, OY, PWp, PHp)`. So the stencil lands m px up and left. drawPenMaskLayer (:2849) has the same blind spot for any padded plate. Controls: the same mask without Motion Blur, and an unmarked mask with Motion Blur, both land exactly on the path, and the blur is shown to engage.
confirmed.fix: Give FM.buildMaskAlpha an origin: pass OX/OY and apply setTransform(s, 0, 0, s, -OX*s, -OY*s) before tracing the path, in both drawPenMaskAt and drawPenMaskLayer.

verdict.reason:
Real. I re-ran the test on port 8904 and it fails with the same numbers: the marked mask shows through 123,82 to 161,122 instead of 140,100 to 180,140. Both controls passed (the same mask without Motion Blur, and an unmarked mask with Motion Blur, land on the path, and the blur visibly smears). The layer only moves in x, so the 18 px shift in y cannot be motion or smear. It can only be a wrong origin.

The code path matches the hunter's evidence:
1. js/fx-browser.js:520 (addMaskFromBrowser) adds `{type:'penmask', maskId}` to every non-adjustment layer. This is what Effects → Mask does for him.
2. In drawLayer (js/compositor.js ~14361), hasPenMask only counts unmarked masks, so the outer drawPenMaskLayer pass is skipped. Then objectblur dispatches outermost, before post-fx (~14421), into drawMotionBlur.
3. drawMotionBlur (~3010-3027) pads the plate by m = min(ceil(travel)+2, PW*0.25) and stamps `plate.__fmOX = -m; plate.__fmOY = -m`. It then draws `tmp`, which strips only objectblur, so the penmask marker renders INSIDE the padded plate.
4. drawPenMaskAt (~2882) gets OX = -m from nestedPlate, which falls through to the final return because rs <= 1.
5. maskAlphaAt / FM.buildMaskAlpha (js/masks.js:129) draws the path with project (0,0) at buffer pixel 0. It only applies scale `s` and knows nothing about the origin.
6. The stencil is then stamped with `octx.drawImage(maskCanvas, OX, OY, ...)` under baseT, which puts project (-m,-m) at buffer pixel 0. So the stencil lands m px up and left.

Preview and export use the same renderScene/drawLayer path, so both are wrong. The mask editor draws the path in project coordinates, so its outline will not match the picture. When the layer stops, the blur declines (no plate), the mask renders in the right place, and the reveal jumps.

He can reach this with normal UI: a shape, text, image or video layer, Effects → Mask, draw it, add Motion Blur (Object), and keyframe the position. Nothing in the fixture is synthetic. It is a plain renderScene of a state the UI creates, and the path is stored in project coordinates, which is how buildMaskAlpha documents it. Two limits on scope: the mover path (shake and the like) sets m = 0 and is not affected, and masks made the unmarked way are not affected. Keyframed transform motion, the common case, is affected. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md or the code comments that makes this offset intended. The fx-browser comment says the marker "renders exactly like an unmarked mask", and this breaks that.

The proposed fix is sound: give buildMaskAlpha the plate origin (translate by -OX*s, -OY*s) in drawPenMaskAt and drawPenMaskLayer. I edited nothing. I stopped the port-8904 server I had started.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug, and a small one. I re-ran the test on port 8904 and it failed the same way: Pixelate 54.7% and RGB Split with Radial 73.3%. All three controls passed. With no effect and with an adjustment Brightness, the zoomed slice matches the whole frame, and the same Pixelate and RGB Split on the image layer also match. So the harness puts the slice in the right place, and only the adjustment path is wrong.

The test sets the same canvas stamps as the real preview. In js/app.js:552, resizeCanvas() sets `__fmCrop = true`, `__fmRS = s` (at least 1) and `__fmOX/__fmOY = crop.x/y` whenever the view is zoomed to 1.35x or more and less than 92% of the frame is visible. Pinch-zooming in reaches that state.

In js/compositor.js, applyAdjustment copies what is on that slice canvas. Pixelate works out its block count as `round(cw/rs/size)` across the slice and draws the blocks from the slice's corner (`drawImage(_adjTmp,0,0,sw,sh,0,0,cw,ch)`). The grid therefore starts wherever the visible area starts, not at the frame's corner. The crop origin is usually fractional (u0*P.width, with an 18% margin), so the blocks land in different places and sample different content than in the export. The grid also moves whenever he pans the zoomed view.

In applyPixelFx, RGB Split centres its radial term on the slice (`cx = W/2, cy = H/2` with W and H being the slice size). With "Toward edges" above 0, the point with no split moves to the middle of whatever he is looking at.

Both effects are allowed on adjustment layers (ADJ_OK in js/fx-registry.js:163), and Pixelate shows it at its defaults (block size 12). The v16.90 fix put effect plates on the whole frame but only touched per-layer effects. The 913.5 clause and its test never mention adjustment layers, and nothing in REQUESTS.md says they were left out on purpose. Yet v16.90 told him "a zoomed view is exactly the export, just closer", and that is false here.

The radial RGB Split case needs "Toward edges" turned up from its default of 0. The default split only differs at the edges of the rendered slice, which are mostly off screen in the 18% margin. So "low" is the right severity, but it is a defect he would see, not a test artefact.

When a Chroma Key or Luma Key is on, the media branch (:14800 and :14806) hands that same ctx.filter string to chromaKey or lumaKey. Those functions apply it to an offscreen canvas the size of the source (w,h = m.width,m.height at :14700): `octx.filter = filterStr; octx.drawImage(src,0,0,w,h)` at :1429. The code then sets ctx.filter to 'none' and draws the keyed source through the render-scale transform. So the blur length is multiplied by the render scale twice. The effective blur is radius × renderScale, when it should be the radius alone. Glow is a drop-shadow length in the same filter string, so it has the same fault.

all.title: A mask added from Effects slides up and left of where he drew it while Motion Blur is on and the layer moves
all.see: He adds Motion Blur to a moving clip and masks it with Effects → Mask. While the clip moves, the masked window shows 17 px left and 18 px up of the outline he drew. The offset grows with speed, up to a quarter of the frame. It snaps back to the right place when the clip stops, so the reveal jumps. It happens the same way in the preview and in the export, and the mask editor's outline does not match the picture.
all.test: HUNT-d a mask added from Effects slides up and left of where he drew it whenever Motion Blur is on and the layer moves. Fails with: with Motion Blur on, the mask he added from Effects shows through 123,82 to 161,122 instead of the 140,100 to 180,140 he drew — it slides 17 px left and 18 px up while the layer moves, in the preview and the export, and snaps back when it stops

The marker is then applied inside that plate by drawPenMaskAt (:2882). nestedPlate returns OX = -m, but maskAlphaAt (:2887, js/masks.js:129) builds the stencil with project (0,0) at pixel 0 and knows nothing of the origin, and it is stamped at the plate origin: :2899 `octx.drawImage(maskCanvas, OX, OY, PWp, PHp)`. So the stencil lands m px up and left. drawPenMaskLayer (:2849) has the same blind spot for any padded plate. Controls: the same mask without Motion Blur, and an unmarked mask with Motion Blur, both land exactly on the path, and the blur is shown to engage.

verdict.reason:
Real. I re-ran the test on port 8904 and it fails with the same numbers: the marked mask shows through 123,82 to 161,122 instead of 140,100 to 180,140. Both controls passed (the same mask without Motion Blur, and an unmarked mask with Motion Blur, land on the path, and the blur visibly smears). The layer only moves in x, so the 18 px shift in y cannot be motion or smear. It can only be a wrong origin.

The code path matches the hunter's evidence:
1. js/fx-browser.js:520 (addMaskFromBrowser) adds `{type:'penmask', maskId}` to every non-adjustment layer. This is what Effects → Mask does for him.
2. In drawLayer (js/compositor.js ~14361), hasPenMask only counts unmarked masks, so the outer drawPenMaskLayer pass is skipped. Then objectblur dispatches outermost, before post-fx (~14421), into drawMotionBlur.
3. drawMotionBlur (~3010-3027) pads the plate by m = min(ceil(travel)+2, PW*0.25) and stamps `plate.__fmOX = -m; plate.__fmOY = -m`. It then draws `tmp`, which strips only objectblur, so the penmask marker renders INSIDE the padded plate.
4. drawPenMaskAt (~2882) gets OX = -m from nestedPlate, which falls through to the final return because rs <= 1.
5. maskAlphaAt / FM.buildMaskAlpha (js/masks.js:129) draws the path with project (0,0) at buffer pixel 0. It only applies scale `s` and knows nothing about the origin.
6. The stencil is then stamped with `octx.drawImage(maskCanvas, OX, OY, ...)` under baseT, which puts project (-m,-m) at buffer pixel 0. So the stencil lands m px up and left.

Preview and export use the same renderScene/drawLayer path, so both are wrong. The mask editor draws the path in project coordinates, so its outline will not match the picture. When the layer stops, the blur declines (no plate), the mask renders in the right place, and the reveal jumps.

He can reach this with normal UI: a shape, text, image or video layer, Effects → Mask, draw it, add Motion Blur (Object), and keyframe the position. Nothing in the fixture is synthetic. It is a plain renderScene of a state the UI creates, and the path is stored in project coordinates, which is how buildMaskAlpha documents it. Two limits on scope: the mover path (shake and the like) sets m = 0 and is not affected, and masks made the unmarked way are not affected. Keyframed transform motion, the common case, is affected. I found nothing in REQUESTS.md or the code comments that makes this offset intended. The fx-browser comment says the marker "renders exactly like an unmarked mask", and this breaks that.

The proposed fix is sound: give buildMaskAlpha the plate origin (translate by -OX*s, -OY*s) in drawPenMaskAt and drawPenMaskLayer. I edited nothing. I stopped the port-8904 server I had started.

Pixelate counts blocks over the slice and anchors them at its corner: :14998 `const sw = Math.max(1, Math.round((cw / rs) / size))` then `a.drawImage(_adjTmp, 0, 0, sw, sh, 0, 0, cw, ch)`. verdict.reason:
This is a real bug, and a small one. I re-ran the test on port 8904 and it failed the same way: Pixelate 54.7% and RGB Split with Radial 73.3%. All three controls passed. With no effect and with an adjustment Brightness, the zoomed slice matches the whole frame, and the same Pixelate and RGB Split on the image layer also match. So the harness puts the slice in the right place, and only the adjustment path is wrong.

The test sets the same canvas stamps as the real preview. In js/app.js:552, resizeCanvas() sets `__fmCrop = true`, `__fmRS = s` (at least 1) and `__fmOX/__fmOY = crop.x/y` whenever the view is zoomed to 1.35x or more and less than 92% of the frame is visible. Pinch-zooming in reaches that state.

In js/compositor.js, applyAdjustment copies what is on that slice canvas. Pixelate works out its block count as `round(cw/rs/size)` across the slice and draws the blocks from the slice's corner (`drawImage(_adjTmp,0,0,sw,sh,0,0,cw,ch)`). The grid therefore starts wherever the visible area starts, not at the frame's corner. The crop origin is usually fractional (u0*P.width, with an 18% margin), so the blocks land in different places and sample different content than in the export. The grid also moves whenever he pans the zoomed view.

In applyPixelFx, RGB Split centres its radial term on the slice (`cx = W/2, cy = H/2` with W and H being the slice size). With "Toward edges" above 0, the point with no split moves to the middle of whatever he is looking at.

Both effects are allowed on adjustment layers (ADJ_OK in js/fx-registry.js:163), and Pixelate shows it at its defaults (block size 12). The v16.90 fix put effect plates on the whole frame but only touched per-layer effects. The 913.5 clause and its test never mention adjustment layers, and nothing in REQUESTS.md says they were left out on purpose. Yet v16.90 told him "a zoomed view is exactly the export, just closer", and that is false here.

The radial RGB Split case needs "Toward edges" turned up from its default of 0. The default split only differs at the edges of the rendered slice, which are mostly off screen in the 18% margin. So "low" is the right severity, but it is a defect he would see, not a test artefact.

The preview has nothing like this. It plays through the media elements with no master gain; the only limiter in `js/audio-fx-live.js` is for clips boosted above 100%. So preview and export really do differ everywhere, not just at the overlap.

The test's levels are realistic:
- The built-in sound effects are scaled to TARGET_PEAK 0.89 (`js/sfx.js`), which matches the test's 0.9 sound effect.
- A song at 0.9 is quieter than a typical commercial master, so real songs would push the peak at least as high.
- Sound effects come in as ordinary 'video' layers carrying a WAV (recorded in #677), which is what the test builds.
- His own measured setups hit the same code. #604 peaked at 1.52 to 1.61, so gain 0.62 to 0.65 and the whole file about 3.7 to 4.1 dB down. #677 was turned down by ×0.853, about 1.4 dB.

Why I don't count this as intended behaviour: the flat turn-down was a Claude decision in v13.80 (#604), not something Ezra asked for. The comment in `js/exporter.js` and the #604 entry defend it by saying a limiter would change how the mix sounds compared with the preview. But a whole-file cut of 1.5 to 5 dB changes it more, and everywhere. The comment's line "Losing 4 dB on a 1.6 peak is inaudible" compares the cut with clipping distortion, not with the preview.

How serious it is: the file is not broken, just quieter. His real setups lost about 1.4 to 4 dB and the test fixture 4.8 dB. He has never complained about quiet exports. Changing it means reversing a documented decision, and the suggested limiter is its own trade-off: it only reshapes the sound where clips overlap. So this is closer to low-medium than medium, and whether to swap in a limiter is a decision to put to him.

all.title: On an iPhone set to silent, the sound-effect preview is silent (and so are reversed clips), because the app never asks iOS to treat its audio as media
all.see: With the phone's ring/silent switch on silent, which is how most iPhones are kept, tapping ▶ on any sound in Add ▸ Audio ▸ Sound effects makes no sound at all, and a reversed clip plays silently, while his ordinary clips still play. That is his #562 complaint (previewing sound effects doesn't work). v12.78 fixed a real exception there, but a desktop can't show this second cause.
all.test: HUNT-e on an iPhone set to silent the sound effect preview makes no sound, because the app never asks for the playback audio session. It fails with: the sound effect previewed through Web Audio with navigator.audioSession left at auto — on an iPhone that is the ambient session, which the ring/silent switch mutes, so on a phone set to silent every ▶ in the sound effects list (and every reversed clip) makes no sound while his other clips still play. The ▶ is pressed with a real mouse click through tests/_cdp.py, and navigator.audioSession is stubbed the way Safari exposes it (type starts at auto). Control: the click reached the preview (its row lit up). It fails at 900 and 380 px and passes when preview() sets the type to playback (throwaway, reverted).
all.evidence: js/sfx.js:644 preview(): liveCtx = FM.audioCtx() (js/sfx.js:651), and the recipe renders into a gain on liveCtx.destination (js/sfx.js:660), so it is Web Audio only with no media element playing. Reversed clips work the same way: js/audio-play.js synthesises AudioBufferSource voices while their elements are paused and muted (js/app.js syncMediaToClock reversed branch). WebKit gives a page that plays only Web Audio the ambient session, which the silent switch mutes, while media elements get the playback session. navigator.audioSession (Safari 16.4+/17) is the fix for this, and there are no matches for audioSession anywhere in js/.
all.fix: Once, when available: `if (navigator.audioSession) navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback'`. Do it at boot, or in FM.audioCtx() when the shared context is created, so the sound-effect preview, reversed clips and the audition all use the playback session. Old Safari needs no fallback: without the API it keeps today's behaviour.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect, but only when the phone is in Silent mode. I re-ran the test on port 8905 and it fails at 900px and at 380px with "navigator.audioSession left at auto". The CONTROL passed on both runs: the real click lit the row.

The test is only a stand-in. It stubs navigator.audioSession and checks that the app sets the type to 'playback'. It cannot hear an iPhone. So I checked the mechanism in WebKit's own code (MediaSessionManagerCocoa.mm, updateSessionState). With no override set, WebKit picks MediaPlayback only when an audio or video element is audible and is playing, preparing to play, or has played audibly since the last interruption. If there is only Web Audio, it picks AmbientSound, and Silent mode mutes that category.

The app always lands in that second case during a preview:
- js/sfx.js:644 preview() plays through FM.audioCtx() into liveCtx.destination. It is Web Audio only, with no media element.
- FM.pause (js/app.js:2314) and media.js:103 leave every clip's element muted whenever playback is stopped, so no element counts as audible while he browses Add ▸ Audio ▸ Sound effects.
- Nothing in js/ or index.html touches audioSession, and there is no silent-audio-element workaround.

Ezra uses an iPhone 16 Pro Max on iOS 26 (REQUESTS.md lines 1498 and 30341). His phone has navigator.audioSession, and Silent mode is an ordinary state he can be in. In that state every ▶ preview is silent. A sound effect he actually adds becomes a video element (FM.loadVideoFile), so it plays when he plays the timeline. That fits his #562 wording, "Previewing sound effects in the sound effect menu doesn't work". v12.78 fixed a different cause, and nothing shows he ever heard a preview on his phone afterwards. This is not something he asked for, and the click is real input on a normal flow.

Caveats:
- It only happens with Silent mode on. We don't know whether he uses it, so "how most iPhones are kept" is an assumption.
- His phone has the Action button, not a ring/silent switch, but Silent mode works the same way.
- The reversed-clip claim is only partly true. The session only drops to Ambient during stretches where no forward clip is audibly playing.

The proposed fix works: WebKit uses categoryOverride() before any other branch, and 'playback' maps to MediaPlayback.

fixed: iPhone preview ignored Mute, levels under 100%, fades and volume keyframes, because iOS won't let a page set el.volume. Test renamed to '690 on an iPhone, where el.volume cannot be set, a muted clip is silent in the preview and a 25 percent clip plays at 25 percent'. Mute now goes through el.muted, which iOS does let a page set. The playback tick (js/app.js syncMediaToClock) mutes the element whenever layerVolume x fadeMul is 0, and FM.play opens a muted layer already muted. For the other levels, js/audio-fx-live.js volumeLocked() checks each element once by writing a level and reading it back. If the level doesn't stick, needsLevel() routes the clip through a Web Audio gain (a new 'L|' level stage with no limiter), but only when its level isn't a flat 100%. setBoost is floored at 0 instead of 1 on those elements, so the gain carries the whole level. Plain clips at 100% keep the native path and never create an audio context. The inspector's volume drag now also updates that stage. WHAT HE HEARS: on the iPhone, Mute, Extract Audio and Remove Vocals now silence the original while he edits, and levels under 100%, fades and volume keyframes can be heard in the preview. Nothing on screen changes. Proof: fails on main (muted clip at level 1.00, native, el.muted false). Separate mutations of the mute half, the level stage and the gain floor each turn it red.

After a stall, the catch-up played a 1x song 1.65 semitones sharp and then left it about 135 ms late. Test renamed to '690 after a 200 ms stall a 1x song keeps its pitch while it catches up, and ends back in step with the picture'. Two changes. (a) New FM.pitchForRate in js/media.js, called from FM.play, setPreviewRate and every tick: preservesPitch is on while the clip's speed x preview rate is 1, so a sync trim becomes a time-stretch. Sped-up clips still resample, as queue 916 asked; the 916.1 tests still pass. (b) New FM._syncMayLearn in js/app.js: the latency learner (the EMA bias) only learns from errors inside the 45 ms dead band. A stall is now corrected instead of absorbed. FM._syncBiasStep takes an optional learn argument and behaves exactly as before when it's left out, so the 493 test is unchanged. Measured after the fix: 0 cents of detune and 33-36 ms left 4.5 s after a 200 ms stall, inside the dead band. Before the fix: 1.65 semitones sharp and 131-152 ms left. WHAT HE HEARS: songs no longer go out of tune when playback falls behind, and they catch fully back up to the picture. The catch-up now takes about 2.5 s at up to +10% tempo with pitch unchanged. Nothing visual. Proof: fails on main. Reverting only the pitch half fails (sharp for about 2.6 s); reverting only the bias half fails (162 ms left).

One short sound effect over a song turned the whole exported song down about 5 dB. Test renamed to '690 one short sound effect over a song turns down only the overlap in the exported file, not the whole song'. I also made it stronger: the song 0.4 s after the overlap must be back at its level, and the overlap must still peak at or below 1.0 in the mix, with a control that the mix really went over 1.2. In js/exporter.js, the whole-file divide in buildAudioMix is replaced by limitMix, a stereo-linked look-ahead limiter written in plain JS. Its gain falls up to 5 ms before an over and recovers at 250 ms per unit of gain (a 0.57 dip comes back in about 0.1 s). Every sample is provably at or below the 0.995 ceiling. It works in 32k-sample blocks so a long export doesn't need a second full-length array on the phone. I didn't use a DynamicsCompressorNode because Chrome's adds make-up gain (about +0.9 dB) to everything, plus a look-ahead delay. New test '690 the export limiter keeps every sample under the ceiling, never jumps its gain at a block seam, and leaves the song away from an over untouched' covers the block seams; mutations that break the carried release state or the look-ahead both fail it. The #604 test still passes. WHAT HE HEARS: exports with overlapping sounds keep the preview's level everywhere except the overlap itself, so they come out louder than before (his #604 setup was about 4 dB down). One text change, in the export report under Settings: the mix-peak line now reads '(limited: x0.573 at the loudest overlap only)' instead of '(turned down x0.573)'. Nothing else visible.

On an iPhone set to silent, the sound-effect preview (and reversed clips) made no sound because the page never asked for the playback audio session. Test renamed to '690 the sound effect preview asks for the playback audio session, so an iPhone set to silent still plays it'. In js/audio-fx.js, new FM.playbackSession() runs on every FM.audioCtx() call and sets navigator.audioSession.type from 'auto' to 'playback'. It never overrides a type the page chose on purpose, and does nothing where the API is missing. To keep the voice recorder safe (a playback override would beat WebKit's play-and-record session for the mic), arm() in js/voice-rec.js hands the session back to 'auto' before asking for the mic. New FM.voiceRec.micLive() (true while a mic track is live or a request is still pending) stops playbackSession from taking it back, and releaseMic() restores playback. New test '690 while the microphone is open the app leaves the audio session to WebKit, and asks for playback again once it is released' uses the real recorder and the suite's fake mic. Four separate mutations of that handover each fail it. WHAT HE HEARS: with the phone on silent, the ▶ previews in Add > Audio > Sound effects and reversed clips now play. Side effect: a sound-effect preview now pauses other apps' music, the way playing a clip already does. Nothing visual.
notFixed: No bug turned out to be wrong; all four were real and are fixed, and no test was deleted.

Sped-up clips (speed or preview rate other than 1x) still resample during a sync catch-up, so they still bend pitch by up to 1.65 semitones while catching up. Because the catch-up now runs to the end instead of stalling at about 40% closed, a 200 ms stall bends a sped-up clip for about 2.5 s instead of about 1.3 s (measured with the pitch half reverted). Only a smaller trim or a declicked seek for pitch-following clips would fix that. I haven't done it; the 1x case (songs) is fixed.

Trade in the sync fix: after the 0.25 s warm-up, any error over 45 ms is now treated as lag, not latency. If an element's output latency were still settling by more than 45 ms after the warm-up (never measured on his phone), the song would end up early by the excess instead of learning it. SYNC_WARMUP exists to make that safe, and the queue-148 tests stay green.

The iPhone fixes (volume and audio session) are proven against WebKit stand-ins (unsettable el.volume that reads 1; a stubbed navigator.audioSession), not on a real iPhone. On the phone, clips whose level isn't a flat 100% now go through MediaElementSource, like effect and boosted clips already did. They inherit that path's known risk: if iOS suspends the audio context, those clips go silent until it resumes.

The export limiter reverses a documented Claude-made decision from #604 (flat divide rather than a limiter). The verdict called that a call to put to Ezra, so he may want to hear an overlap export before this ships.

Related slice run: 'the quality ladder sheds pixels under sustained load (queue 202)' failed on its own in the '?only=speed' slice, and it fails the same way on main's sources. Its control says the scene is only 35 ms a frame, so it isn't struggling on this machine. It passed in both full suites, so it's an isolation or machine artefact, not something these changes caused.

confirmed.title: With the phone storage full, opening another project throws away everything since the last save
confirmed.see: When the phone is full, the app shows 'Storage full — autosave paused' once and lets him keep editing. Later he goes Home and opens a different project (or presses + Create). Everything he did after that one toast is gone. Nothing warns him when he switches, there is nothing to undo, and when he comes back the project is the older version.
confirmed.test: HUNT-f with the phone storage full, opening another project silently throws away everything since the last save. Fails with: with the phone storage full, opening another project threw away the text layer he had just added — coming back shows only [HUNTf saved]. The only warning was the one toast when the first save failed; nothing was said at the switch (no question asked, toasts: 1)
confirmed.evidence: js/storage.js:2124 in FM.projects.open: `FM.storage.flushSync(); this.touchCurrent(true);` ignores the return value. flushSync -> writeScene (js/storage.js:60-73) returns false when setItem throws QuotaExceededError. open() then carries on: FM.releaseProjectMedia, `FM.scene.layers = []` (js/storage.js:2147), `await FM.storage.load()` for the other id, and `FM.history.reset()`. create() (js/storage.js:2158) has the same unchecked flush. The warning latch (_quotaWarned, js/storage.js:86-90) has already been used, so no toast appears. The template and element save-back paths already refuse on a failed flush (js/storage.js:2824, 3023); the ordinary project switch does not.
confirmed.fix: In open() and create(), check flushSync(). If it returns false, stop before any teardown: keep the current project open, then either return false with a toast saying the project could not be saved and should be kept via Save project file, or use FM.ask to offer 'Leave anyway / Stay'. A tested sketch that returns false with a toast makes the test pass.

verdict.reason: I re-ran the test on port 8906 and it fails the same way the hunter reported: coming back to project A shows only [HUNTf saved], with 1 toast and no question asked. The code path matches the claim. In js/storage.js:2124, FM.projects.open() calls FM.storage.flushSync() and ignores its result. flushSync returns writeScene()'s false when setItem throws QuotaExceededError (lines 60-73). open() then carries on with the teardown anyway. It releases the project's media, empties FM.scene.layers (line 2147), loads the other project and resets history. The unsaved in-memory edits are gone with no undo. create() at line 2157 has the same unchecked flush. The only warning is the once-per-streak toast in warnQuota (lines 86-90), which has already been used by the time he switches. Home's card taps (home.js:2081, 2205) call projects.open directly, and nothing else checks for unsaved work. A person can reach this state: the toast exists because a heavy project's JSON outgrew the roughly 5MB localStorage quota (#15). The app's own template and element save-back paths already refuse on a failed flush (lines 2824, 3023), so the ordinary switch is the one path that doesn't. REQUESTS.md records an earlier hunt that found 'storage full mid-edit' clean. That hunt only covered staying in the project. It did not cover switching, and nothing in REQUESTS.md says he wanted switching to skip the question. The fixture is a fair stand-in. It refuses only A's document key, but a really full store would refuse more writes, and none of them would save the in-memory scene before it is emptied. The ask stub returning false only matters once a fix exists. One point for whoever writes the fix: flushSync also returns false when the tab is stale (a newer copy of the project was saved elsewhere, in another tab). There, discarding the local edits is deliberate, so a fix should stop the switch only on a quota failure.

confirmed.title: Replacing a clip twice, then undoing twice, does not bring the original back; it is deleted, and redo shows the wrong clip
confirmed.see: He uses Replace media… on a photo or video, doesn't like the result, and replaces it again. Then he presses undo twice to get his original back. The layer's settings go back, but the clip still shows his second pick. The original has been deleted from the project, because the next save writes the second pick over it. If he then redoes twice, the clip claims to be his last pick but still shows the second one.
confirmed.test: HUNT-f replacing a clip twice and pressing undo twice does not bring his original back — it is deleted, and redo shows the wrong clip too. Fails with: he replaced a photo twice, then pressed undo twice to get his original back: the settings went back but the clip still shows his SECOND pick (q915a-hfSECOND-….png), and the saved copy is now q915a-hfSECOND-….png — the original photo is gone from the project for good
confirmed.evidence: js/storage.js:471-479 stashPrevMedia writes a single slot `'prev:' + id`, so the second replace (js/app.js:4135-4138) overwrites the original with the first replacement. js/app.js:4150-4153 removes the library tile that pointed at the original. js/app.js:4086-4101 restoreReplacedMedia only handles `live.rev > want` and needs `prev.rev === want`: on the second undo prev.rev is 1 and want is 0, so it does nothing. Redo never restores anything, because it skips when live.rev <= want. The next save (js/storage.js:535-541) then writes the second pick over the layer's record with rev 0. The test drives the real FM.replaceMedia through its own hidden file input.
confirmed.fix: Stash one entry per revision (for example 'prev:<id>:<rev>'), and have restoreReplacedMedia work in both directions. Before swapping, stash the live file under its own rev, then take the stash for the wanted rev. That way both undo and redo restore the right file. The boot sweep already clears 'prev:' keys. A sketch of exactly this makes the test pass.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I served the worktree on port 8906 and ran the test with ?only=HUNT-f replacing a clip twice. It failed exactly as reported: after two undos the clip still shows q915a-hfSECOND-….png, and FM.storage.readMedia(id) returns the SECOND file too. The test's control check passed, so a single undo still brings the previous file back; only the two-step case breaks.

The code explains it, and it isn't a timing problem:
- js/storage.js:472-479 `stashPrevMedia` keeps one `prev:<id>` slot per layer.
- The first replace stashes A with rev 0. The second replace (js/app.js:4135-4138) stashes B with rev 1, which overwrites A.
- The first replace also dropped A's library tile (js/app.js:4171-4173). The save after it wrote B over the layer key, because planBlobWrites uses layer.mediaRev and the stored rev differs. After the second replace, the stash slot was the only copy of A left anywhere.
- First undo: want=1, the live file is at rev 2, and the stash is B at rev 1, so B comes back. That part works.
- Second undo: want=0, the live file is at rev 1, and the stash is still B at rev 1. The check `prev.rev !== want` (js/app.js:4094) skips it. The layer goes back to mediaRev 0 but keeps showing B, then markDirty and autosave write B to disk with rev 0. A is gone for good.
- Redo is broken as well: js/app.js:4091 skips whenever `live.rev <= want`, so redo never swaps a file in. C has already been overwritten on disk by B, and C's library tile points at the layer key, which now holds B.

It isn't an artefact of the test:
- The test calls the real FM.replaceMedia, the same function the layer ⋯ menu's "Replace media…" item uses (js/app.js:4542) and the template-fill Replace button uses (js/template-fill.js:249).
- The only synthetic step is filling the handler's own hidden file input through DataTransfer and firing change. The handler just reads input.files, so that matches a real pick.
- Picking twice then pressing undo twice is an ordinary thing for him to do.
- He never asked for this behaviour. Queue #829 exists to stop "pick the wrong file and the original is gone". The one-slot bound was chosen to limit storage and never mentions losing the original after two replaces. Two wrong picks cause the very loss #829 was meant to prevent.

Severity HIGH is fair: his original photo or video is permanently deleted while undo looks like it worked, because the layer's settings revert.

confirmed.see: He asks the Director for a scene. It takes most of a minute with a real key, so he closes the panel (✕ works while it runs), goes Home and opens another project. The Director finishes inside that other project and saves it there: captions, shapes and a camera he never added. The camera takes over that project's whole view. The project he asked for keeps only the first part of the build. The no-key 'watch the demo' run does the same thing.
confirmed.test: HUNT-f the AI Director keeps building into whatever project is open — switch projects mid-build and the other project gets its layers. Fails with: the AI Director was still building when he opened another project, and it finished INSIDE that project: 4 layers he never made (Captions text, Shape shape, Shape shape, Camera camera) were added to it and saved, while the project he asked for kept only the start of the build
confirmed.evidence: js/ai.js:131-243 generateScene awaits call() for the interpreter, planner, each builder and the critic, and after each await it writes to FM.scene, which is whatever project is open by then: `FM.scene.project.aiIntent = intent` (:158), `FM.aiOps.applyOps(plan.scaffoldOps, refMap)` (:169), `FM.aiOps.applyOps((r.out && r.out.ops) || [], refMap)` in runBuilder (:188), then `FM.history.commit()` (:234), which autosaves into the other project. verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test on port 8906 and got the same failure. Four layers the Director built (Captions text, Shape, Shape, Camera) ended up in project B and were saved to disk. Project A kept only the scaffold. I read the code path in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ezrasmith-Claude-FreeMotion/fde0eeaf-7d73-45b8-9f83-7761553e344d/scratchpad/wt/hunt-f and it is a real defect a person can reach:

That covers aiIntent (:158), the scaffold applyOps (:169), the builders' applyOps inside runBuilder (:188), the critic, and the final FM.history.commit (:234), which autosaves. Nothing records which project the run started in. aborted() only reads state.abort.

confirmed.title: After one storage warning, a clip that cannot be saved says nothing and comes back blank after a reload
confirmed.see: On a nearly full phone, the one 'Not enough storage to save that media' toast of the session can go on something he never added, such as the project card's thumbnail, which autosave refreshes. Later, after clips have been saving fine, the phone fills again and he adds a photo or video. It plays normally, but it was never saved, and nothing tells him. The next time the app opens, that clip is blank.
confirmed.test: HUNT-f once one storage warning has shown, a clip that cannot be saved says nothing and comes back blank after a reload. Fails with: the photo he just added could not be saved because the phone is full, and NOTHING said so — the only storage warning of the session had already been used up (here by a card thumbnail). It plays now and will come back blank the next time the app opens. Toasts at the time: []
confirmed.evidence: js/storage.js:224-234: `let _storeWarned = false; function warnStore(e) { … if (_storeWarned || !FM.toast) return; _storeWarned = true; …}`. Nothing ever sets it back to false, not even after a successful write. Every IndexedDB writer calls it: idbPut (:220), idbPutSharedOnce and idbPutPointer (:187-210), and putThumb (:1933), which touchCurrent calls on autosave (:2099). save() ignores the result of the clip write (js/storage.js:540, `if (!asPtr) await idbPut(...)`), so the clip stays in memory and looks fine until a reload. The #912 audit mentioned 'shown once per session' in passing, but the latch was never changed.
confirmed.fix: Reset _storeWarned after any successful idbPut, so the next failure after space comes back warns again. Warn about a failed clip or scene-media write every time, or at least once per clip, and never let a thumbnail or cache write use up the warning.
